sources.title: Georges Neaime, Geodesic normal forms and Hecke algebras for the complex reflection groups G(de,e,n)
sources.locator: §6, printed pp. 32–38, Theorem 6.1 and Lemmas 6.2–6.15; the multiplicative G(r,1,n) rank-one specialization and the present finite-field quotient calculations are proved locally.
sources.reading_verification: Fetched and inspected the full 437 KB PDF and its complete §6 in the extracted text. The section gives the generator-closed normal-word reductions and the cyclotomic G(d,1,n) basis route. Its coefficient normalization and some cited rank-two cases differ from the present R,Q,u convention; it is a source for the route only, while the local claims and corrections are proved in their stated convention.

contents.name: Cyclotomic normal-word span for G(d,1,n)
contents.support: The source supplies the normal-word induction pattern. The current published carrier writes the coefficient extension, corrected commutation range, quadratic coefficients, finite parabolic reductions, and all nine generator cases locally; no source citation substitutes for those arguments.

contents.name: Rank-one repeated-parameter specialization
contents.locator: §6, Theorem 6.1; comparison with the presentation in §2
contents.support: The paper supplies the multiplicative cyclotomic presentation context. The rank-one monic quotient, its basis, and the nonzero nilpotent at a repeated root are derived locally from the presentation.

sources.title: Jun Hu and Andrew Mathas, Seminormal forms and cyclotomic quiver Hecke algebras of type A
sources.locator: §3.1–3.2, PDF pp. 14–20: content separation, Gelfand–Zetlin idempotents, seminormal coefficients, and the explicit braid-coefficient comparison.
sources.reading_verification: Fetched and inspected the full 718 KB PDF and the complete relevant sections. The paper proves content-sequence separation under its stated separation condition, constructs the interpolation idempotents, and compares all local braid coefficients. Its Jucys–Murphy normalization is not identical to the multiplicative Q,u normalization here; the old published carriers state and prove their own conversion and boundary cases.

contents.name: Content separation and generic seminormal projectors
contents.locator: §3.1, Lemma 3.3, Proposition 3.4 and formula (3.5), PDF pp. 14–15
contents.support: The paper provides an independent treatment of separated content sequences and spectral projectors. The current item proves the multipartition box-poset separation and the required formulas in its own multiplicative normalization.

sources.title: Andrew Mathas, Cyclotomic quiver Hecke algebras of type A (full lecture notes)
sources.locator: §1.1, §1.4 and §1.6, printed pp. 3–11: the Ariki–Koike convention, multipartitions/tableaux, content separation, and seminormal matrix units.
sources.reading_verification: Fetched and inspected the full 1.2 MB lecture-note PDF and the complete cited sections. The notes explicitly distinguish the multiplicative Ariki–Koike algebra from the degenerate algebra at v²=1, define multipartitions and standard tableaux, and give the separated-content projector and seminormal-basis construction. The local page preserves that normalization warning and supplies its own proofs.

contents.name: Ariki–Koike normalization, multipartitions, and seminormal basis context
contents.support: The notes independently document the combinatorial and normalization conventions. Their formulas are not imported at singular normalization values; the current definition proves its content separation claims locally.

contents.name: Repeated cyclotomic parameters and rank-one algebra
contents.locator: §1.1, especially the distinction between multiplicative and degenerate presentations
contents.support: The notes support the parameter-convention distinction only. The polynomial quotient and its nilpotent basis are proved locally.

contents.name: Ordinary RSK insertion and reverse deletion
contents.support: The lecture notes provide the ordinary insertion and reverse-deletion theorem. The current item proves componentwise relabelling, the colored inverse, and the r^n n! count locally.
